title: Washington's 3rd Congressional District election, 2026
description: Washington's 3rd Congressional District, encompassing Vancouver and southwest Washington, is the most competitive congressional district in the state with a Cook PVI of R+2. Incumbent Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, first elected in 2022, is seeking a third term in a district that also voted for Donald Trump in 2024. The race is expected to be a top national target for Republicans, with state Senate Minority Leader John Braun emerging as the leading Republican challenger after receiving former President Trump's endorsement. The August 4 top-two primary will narrow the field of eight candidates to two for the November general election, with control of the U.S. House potentially hinging on this battleground seat.
polling_note: No publicly available independent opinion polls were found for this race as of the search date. A Facebook post referenced a 'jungle primary poll' but no credible pollster or methodology was identified.

candidates.name: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
candidates.summary: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Washington's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2022. A small business owner who co-owns an auto repair shop in Portland, she has positioned herself as a moderate Democrat, often breaking with her party on issues such as immigration and censure votes. She was re-elected in 2024 with 51.7% of the vote, making her one of only 13 Democrats to win a district carried by Donald Trump.

candidates.name: John Braun
candidates.summary: John Braun is the Washington State Senate Minority Leader, representing the 20th Legislative District since 2013. A retired U.S. Navy submarine officer with 31 years of military service, he has been endorsed by former President Donald Trump in his bid to unseat Gluesenkamp Perez. Braun has raised approximately $1 million and is considered the leading Republican contender in the race.

candidates.name: Brent Hennrich
candidates.summary: Brent Hennrich is a progressive Democratic candidate challenging incumbent Marie Gluesenkamp Perez from the left. A stay-at-home father who previously ran for this seat in 2022, he has criticized Perez for her support of the SAVE Act and Laken Riley Act. Hennrich raised nearly $100,000 in the first quarter of 2026, positioning himself as an anti-establishment progressive alternative.

candidates.name: Antony Barran
candidates.summary: Antony Barran is an oyster farm owner and entrepreneur running under the Cascade Party banner. Originally entered the race as a Republican, he switched to the newly formed Cascade Party, which seeks to disrupt the two-party dynamic in Washington. Barran advocates for small business growth and rural renewal.

forecast.rationale: Washington's 3rd is a genuine battleground: the district has a slight Republican baseline (Cook PVI R+2) and voted for Donald Trump in 2024, making it a prime GOP target. But incumbent Democrat Marie Gluesenkamp Perez has already demonstrated unusual crossover appeal here, winning in 2022 and again in 2024 with 51.7% despite the district's Republican tilt, and incumbency gives her a modest structural advantage. Republicans appear to have a credible top challenger in John Braun, a well-known state legislative leader with significant fundraising and a Trump endorsement, so the race cannot be rated beyond a narrow edge. With no credible public polling, this forecast relies on fundamentals rather than direct voter measurement, which keeps confidence low and suggests only the slightest Democratic advantage at this stage. The August 4 top-two primary will provide the first real electoral signal on candidate strength and turnout dynamics.
